answer: Sequential puzzle chain. Each identity must solve a unique cipher puzzle derived from the prior solver's output, forming a single serial chain. A quill signature (unique human timing pattern) must accompany each solve. To register N identities, an attacker must solve all N puzzles sequentially and forge N distinct timing patterns, costing weeks of serial compute and biometric spoofing per identity. Parallelism is impossible because each puzzle depends on the last. The bridge between identities is the chain itself: skip one solve and downstream puzzles become unsolvable.
